How to read this & what to watch for

  • Bars are relative by default. Length is scaled to the highest line for that gene (RNA on a log10 basis; protein on its linear log2 scale). Switch to Absolute to compare magnitude across genes. The printed number is always the measured value.
  • RNA vs protein are different assays and units — TPM (within-sample-normalised transcript abundance) vs TMT log2 relative protein abundance. Compare them by rank/pattern, not by matching numbers. TMT compresses ratios, so small protein-bar differences can understate real ones.
  • "n.d." = not detected in that assay. Protein has structural block-missingness (~9% of values): a protein absent from a whole TMT plex is missing for every line in that plex, not necessarily biologically absent. Absence of protein is weaker evidence than presence.
  • Histotype ≠ source site ≠ TMT plex are partially confounded (e.g. all clear-cell lines come from one site). A difference that tracks subtype may partly reflect batch/site — treat cross-subtype contrasts as hypotheses.
  • Gene identifiers: RNA is keyed by Ensembl gene ID (release 105) and mapped to symbols; where several Ensembl genes share a symbol the highest-mean-TPM gene is shown (its Ensembl ID is listed under the gene name). Protein is symbol-keyed; ~2.6% of proteins have no RNA match here (symbol-synonym differences), and vice-versa — shown honestly as "not in RNA/protein".
  • One library/replicate per line. These are single measurements; a few lines carry subtype ‡ label conflicts (flagged when shown). Values are rounded for display.

Cook Lab · Ottawa Hospital Research Institute / University of Ottawa · OvCAN human ovarian cancer cell-line multi-omic resource. Data embedded client-side (data.js, gzipped); no server or network calls. Regenerate with python3 app/build_payload.py.
